ED Recovery Calling Playbook
Everything a Logicall agent needs to start placing high-intent recovery calls for the
two new ED telehealth formulas — products, per-stage scripts, objections, and the
compliance lines that matter most in this category.
FORMULAS STAGE LANGUAGE
QuattroRx · TriShot Dosage + Checkout English (US)
Executive Summary
01
This vertical launches the Standard Meds Erectile Dysfunction (ED) line — two physician-
prescribed formulas that split by how the patient wants to treat it: QuattroRx (daily) and
TriShot (on-demand). Logicall handles the one recoverable stage in this funnel — the
combined Dosage + Checkout abandon — for both formulas.
ONE COMBINED STAGE — DOSAGE AND CHECKOUT ARE THE SAME PAGE
Page 1 of 9

In this funnel there's no separate "pick a plan, then pay" step: the product and the payment live
on the same page, at a single price. So there's one high-intent recovery moment — a lead who
reached that page and didn't complete payment. They already finished the assessment, saw
the price, and stopped one click short. This is the closest-to-"yes" segment there is; treat
every one of these calls as priority.
IMPORTANT — QUIZ ABANDONMENT IS NOT RECOVERABLE
Both funnels capture name, email and phone only on the last quiz question. If a lead drops
before that, we have zero contact data. There is no "Quiz Abandon" recovery. The recoverable
stage starts once a lead finishes the quiz and lands on the Dosage + Checkout page.
The recoverable stage
1. Dosage + Checkout Abandon — finished the quiz, reached the combined dosage-and-
checkout page, saw the price, didn't complete payment. (Pricing-active call.)
The Two Formulas at a Glance
02
Read these two cards before your first call. They split by intent: daily & ready vs. on-demand
& strongest. Everything you'll anchor on lives here.
QuattroRx
DAILY ED · CHEWABLE · 4-IN-1
A physician-prescribed daily chewable combining Tadalafil 5 mg and Vardenafil HCl 5 mg (two
PDE5 inhibitors) with Vitamin D3 200 IU and Vitamin K2 1 mg for vascular support.
Compounded at an FDA-registered pharmacy.
MECHANISM Low daily doses of two PDE5 inhibitors keep a steady baseline in the bloodstream —
you're ready without timing a pill to the moment. D3 + K2 support endothelial and
nitric-oxide vascular health, treating the underlying cause, not just the event.
BEST FOR Men who want spontaneity — no planning, ready anytime — and want to treat ED as
an ongoing vascular-health program.
FORM Chewable gum — discreet, no water, buccal absorption.
TONE Reassuring, confidence-restoring. "Get back to ready — without planning your life
around a pill."
Page 2 of 9

TriShot
ON-DEMAND ED · TABLET · 3-IN-1
A physician-prescribed on-demand tablet combining Tadalafil 20 mg, Sildenafil 70 mg, and
Apomorphine 4 mg — two blood-flow pathways plus a central (brain-level) trigger. Compounded
at an FDA-registered pharmacy.
MECHANISM Sildenafil brings fast onset; tadalafil brings a long window. Apomorphine works
centrally — it triggers the arousal signal in the brain, a different pathway than blood-
flow-only pills. Three mechanisms = the most complete response.
BEST FOR Men who take it when they need it, and men for whom a single-ingredient pill
(Viagra/Cialis alone) hasn't been enough.
FORM Tablet — take on demand.
TONE Confident, discreet, matter-of-fact. "The strongest response we make — for when one
ingredient hasn't cut it."
Pricing
QUATTRORX — DAILY
MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION
$99
first month
then $149/mo
One option — a monthly subscription: $99 the first month, then $149/mo. No plan choice on the call;
the dosage-and-checkout page sells this single price.
TRISHOT — ON-DEMAND
BASE OFFER · 6 DOSES
$99
first month
then $149/mo
The dosage-and-checkout page sells the 6-dose base: $99 the first month, then $149/mo — same
headline price as QuattroRx. There are also two quantity upgrades in the flow that you're welcome to
offer once the base is secured:
Order bump (on the checkout page) → step up to 12 doses for $164
Page 3 of 9

Upsell (after purchase) → step up to 18 doses for $229
BOTH FORMULAS — SAME HEADLINE PRICE
QuattroRx and TriShot both lead with the same offer: $99 the first month, then $149/mo.
TriShot also has an order bump ($164 / 12 doses) and an upsell ($229 / 18 doses) —
recovering the base checkout is always your #1 job, but if the call's going well you're welcome
to offer the upgrade too. See §3 for how.
OFFERS MAY VARY OVER TIME
Standard Meds continuously tests and rotates offers, so a lead may see plans or prices
different from the ones above. The live dosage-and-checkout page is always the source of
truth.
Per-Stage Playbook
03
One combined stage — dosage and checkout are the same page, so there's a single recovery
card. Openers and discovery questions are a guide, not a script to read verbatim — adjust to
your own voice. Stay discreet: this is a sensitive category.
THE ONE RECOVERABLE STAGE
Dosage + Checkout Abandon
The lead finished the assessment and landed on the combined dosage-and-checkout page —
they saw the product, saw the single price, and stopped before completing payment. This is the
hottest segment in the funnel: they know the product and the price, and stopped one decision
short. The objection is almost never "tell me about the product." It's "is it worth it," or a small
friction at payment. Don't re-sell from scratch — just remove the friction and close.
GOAL
Send the dosage/checkout link via SMS
AVG CALL
≤ 5 min, ideally < 3
PRICING POSTURE
Active — one price, just close
OPENER (≤ 15 SEC)
Page 4 of 9

"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} calling from Standard Meds. You completed your
health assessment recently and I saw you got all the way to the checkout page but didn't
finish — I wanted to check in — is this a good time for a quick call?"
DISCOVERY QUESTION (≤ 45 SEC)
"I noticed you got all the way through the assessment and to the page, but didn't complete
it — was there a specific question, or anything that came up I can help with?"
ADDRESS — MOST COMMON PATTERNS
"Is it worth it / price" → It's one straightforward price — no tiers to weigh. Reinforce
the value: a physician-reviewed, compounded program, not a gas-station pill. Use
the brand anchors below.
"I saw $99 but it's charging $149" (both formulas) → Clarify calmly: the $99 is
the first month, an intro price; it's a monthly subscription that renews at $149/mo
after that. Nothing hidden — the first month is simply discounted. (See §4 for the full
script.)
Payment friction / "card was declined" → Reassure, suggest trying another card;
the link sends them right back to the same page with everything saved.
"Let me think" → Acknowledge. Offer the link so they can come back ready —
nothing is lost.
Privacy / "will this show on my statement?" → The charge shows up as
STANDARDMEDS (or the shortened STNDMEDS on some statements) — never the
product name. Reassure: discreet billing and plain, unmarked packaging.
BRAND-SPECIFIC TANGIBLE ANCHORS (USE WHEN PRICE COMES UP)
QUATTRORX — ANCHOR ANGLES
vs. planning around a pill every time → daily = always ready, spontaneity restored
Two PDE5 pathways + vascular support (D3/K2) — treats the cause, not just the moment
Discreet chewable, no water, no "wait 30–60 minutes"
vs. buying generic Viagra + supplements separately → one compounded, physician-reviewed
program
TRISHOT — ANCHOR ANGLES
Three mechanisms vs. the one in Viagra/Cialis — fast onset and long window and a central
trigger
Built for men where a single-ingredient pill hasn't been enough
Page 5 of 9

Apomorphine works in the brain — addresses the signal, not just blood flow
Real compounded prescription from an FDA-registered pharmacy
CLOSE
"Can I send you the link right now so you can finish up where you left off? Takes a
minute."
ACTION ON YES
Trigger SMS send with the dosage/checkout page link. Verbally confirm: "Sent — you
should see the text any moment. Let me know when it comes through."
OPTIONAL — UPGRADE OFFERS (TRISHOT, SECONDARY)
The base close always comes first — that's the win. But once the patient is committed
to the 6-dose base (or clearly enthusiastic), you're welcome to offer the upgrades that
are already built into the checkout flow:
Order bump → 12 doses for $164:"Since you're getting set up — a lot of guys go
with the 12-dose option at $164; it's better value per dose and you're covered longer.
Want me to set that one up instead?"
Upsell → 18 doses for $229: after checkout an 18-dose option shows at $229 — if
they took the 12 and they're keen, it's a natural step up.
Guardrails: never let an upgrade jeopardize the base sale, keep it to one soft offer, and if they
say no, drop it immediately and lock in the base. QuattroRx has no upgrade — base only.
VOICEMAIL SCRIPT
"Hi {first name}, this is {agent name} from Standard Meds. You completed your
assessment recently and I wanted to make sure you had everything you needed to finish.
I'll send a text with your link so you can take a look when it's convenient. Take care!"
Objection Library
04
The full bench of rebuttals. These are guidance, not scripts to read verbatim. ED is a sensitive
category — stay warm, professional, and non-judgmental throughout. When a question turns
medical (interactions, heart conditions, dosing), defer to the physician review — do not
advise.
Page 6 of 9

Shared — both formulas
Q "How do I know this isn't a scam?"
A "Completely fair question. These are real compounded prescriptions — they go through an FDA-
registered pharmacy, they're third-party tested, and a licensed physician reviews every patient's
assessment before anything is prescribed."
Q "I saw $99, but it's charging me $149 — what's going on?"
A "Good catch, and nothing's off. The $99 is an intro price for your first month. It's a monthly
subscription, so after that first month it renews at the regular $149 a month — you're just getting the
first one at a discount. You can manage or cancel it anytime; nothing is locked in." (Applies to both
formulas — same $99→$149 base. If asked "so it's every month?" — "Yes, it's a monthly refill so you
never run out; the physician sets the plan.")
Q "Is this discreet? I don't want anyone to know."
A "Absolutely — that's how the whole program is built. Everything happens through a private patient
portal, the packaging is plain and unmarked, and the charge shows on your statement as
STANDARDMEDS (or the shortened STNDMEDS) — never the product name. No one sees anything but
you."
Q "Does my insurance cover it?"
A "This is a cash-pay compounded telehealth program, so it doesn't run through insurance — which is
actually what keeps it private and lets us compound the exact formula."
Q "I need to talk to my doctor first."
A "Of course — that's reasonable. And a licensed physician is part of this: they review your health
assessment before anything is approved, and they'll flag anything that isn't a fit. If it helps, I can send
you the link so you have all the details in front of you for that conversation."
QUATTRORX — DAILY
Q "Why would I take something every day? I only need it sometimes."
A "Great question — that's exactly the choice between our two formulas. The daily one keeps a steady
low dose in your system so you're ready anytime, no planning, no timing a pill to the moment. It also
works on the underlying vascular health over time. If you'd rather take something only when you need it,
the on-demand formula is built for that instead."
Q "Is it safe to take an ED medication every day?"
A "Daily low-dose tadalafil is a well-established, widely-used approach — the doses here are specifically
kept low for daily use. That said, the physician reviews your full health assessment before approving
anything, which is exactly what makes sure it's right for you."
Q "What are the vitamins for?"
Page 7 of 9

A "The Vitamin D3 and K2 support your vascular and circulatory health — the blood-flow side of the
equation. It's part of treating the root cause rather than just the moment, which is the whole idea of the
daily formula."
Q "How is a chewable different from a pill?"
A "It absorbs through the mouth, so it's discreet, needs no water, and gets into your system efficiently.
Some men just prefer it to swallowing a tablet every day."
TRISHOT — ON-DEMAND
Q "How is this different from Viagra or Cialis?"
A "Viagra and Cialis are each a single ingredient that works on blood flow. TriShot combines both of
those pathways — the fast onset of one and the long window of the other — plus a third ingredient,
apomorphine, that works in the brain. So it addresses more than just blood flow. It's built to be the most
complete response we make."
Q "What is apomorphine? I've never heard of it."
A "It's a centrally-acting ingredient — meaning it works in the brain to help trigger the arousal signal,
rather than only in the blood vessels like the standard pills. For a lot of men, that's the piece a blood-
flow-only pill was missing."
Q "Viagra/Cialis alone hasn't worked for me."
A "That's actually who this formula is designed for. Because it combines two blood-flow ingredients with
a brain-level trigger, it addresses cases where a single-ingredient pill wasn't enough. The physician
reviews your history to confirm it's the right step for you."
Q "Is it safe to combine two of these together?"
A "It's compounded and dosed by an FDA-registered pharmacy specifically for this combination, and a
licensed physician reviews your health assessment before it's ever approved. That review is exactly
where safety is confirmed for you."
Q "I get headaches / flushing from Viagra."
A "That's worth raising in your assessment — the physician can factor your tolerance into the formula. I
can't adjust dosing myself, but that's precisely the kind of thing the review is there for."
Q "How is this different from BlueChew or the other online ones?"
A "Most of those are a single ingredient in a chewable. TriShot is three mechanisms in one — two blood-
flow pathways plus a central trigger — as a real compounded prescription, physician-reviewed, and
third-party tested."
HARD LINE — MEDICAL QUESTIONS ARE NOT YOURS TO ANSWER
If a lead mentions nitrates, heart medication, chest pain, blood pressure medication,
recent heart attack/stroke, or any drug they're taking and asks whether it's safe to combine
Page 8 of 9

— do not advise, do not reassure with a yes. Say: "That's an important question, and it's
exactly what the physician reviews in your assessment before anything is approved. I'm not
able to give medical advice on that, but the review is built to catch it." Then move on. See §5.
Compliance & Operational Rules
05
The universal rules from your first Standard Meds playbook (v1) still apply in full — this section
covers only what's different or elevated for ED. In this category, drug-interaction safety is a
real risk: a bad call can cost a license, a patient's trust, or their health. Read the red callout
twice.
#1 RULE — THE ED-SPECIFIC LINE THAT MATTERS MOST
PDE5 medications (the class both formulas are built on) can be dangerous when combined
with nitrates or certain blood-pressure and heart medications. You are never to assess,
advise on, or reassure a patient about any drug interaction, heart condition, or dosing question.
Every such question routes to one answer: "the physician reviews that in your assessment
before anything is approved." This protects the patient and it protects the program.
New or elevated for ED
Route ALL medical questions to review
Any interaction / heart / blood-pressure / dosing question → "the physician reviews that." Zero exceptions
— this is ED's number-one rule (see the red callout above). In this category it can be a safety event, not
just a policy slip.
Stay discreet & non-judgmental
ED is a sensitive category. Professional, matter-of-fact tone. Never make the patient feel awkward for the
topic — it costs the call.
